models.description: Built for quick smoke tests and verifying Maguna on low-RAM machines. Much weaker than any larger instruct model here for nuanced writing, German detail, or multi-step reasoning—use it to validate the pipeline, not for daily quality work.

Meta’s compact instruct model: strong everyday English and German following with sensible refusals. Beats tiny 1–2B models on coherence, but lags 7B+ picks (Mistral, Qwen 7B) on subtle style, long reasoning chains, and dense technical prose.
models.license_note: Llama 3.2 Community License Agreement — see HF model card.

models.description: Mistral’s general-purpose 7B instruct: crisp answers and reliable EN/DE behavior for drafting, Q&A, and translation-style prompts. A safe mid-weight default; trades away the peak reasoning and breadth of Qwen 14B or R1-style models on the hardest analytical tasks.
models.license_note: Apache-2.0 — see Mistral model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: Same Mistral 7B v0.3 weights as the Q4 build, with a higher-bit quant for slightly sharper outputs when RAM allows. Marginal quality gain over Q4_K_M for noticeably more disk and memory—skip if you are tight on resources.
models.license_note: Apache-2.0 — see Mistral model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: DeepSeek distilled a reasoning-heavy style into an 8B Llama-format model—strong for step-by-step analysis, math-like problems, and “show your work” answers. Often too verbose for short spelling fixes or tight translations compared to Mistral or Qwen instruct lines.
models.license_note: MIT — DeepSeek R1 distill; see HF model card.

models.description: Same R1-distill behavior as the Q4 file with a heavier quant for a bit more precision when you have headroom. Still biased toward long, reflective replies—avoid for ultra-short modes unless you trim prompts heavily.
models.license_note: MIT — DeepSeek R1 distill; see HF model card.

models.description: Alibaba’s Qwen 2.5 instruct line is a standout 7B all-rounder with strong multilingual and tool-style discipline. Punches above Llama 3.2 3B on difficult prompts, but the 14B Qwen in this catalog still wins on hardest reasoning and long-form consistency if your machine can run it.
models.license_note: Apache-2.0 — Qwen2.5; see Alibaba model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: The largest dense instruct model in this catalog: best overall bet for difficult instructions, drafting, and mixed EN/DE quality when RAM and CPU throughput allow. Only downsides are footprint and latency versus smaller checkpoints—not worth it on very low-end hardware.
models.license_note: Apache-2.0 — Qwen2.5; see Alibaba model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: Code-tuned Qwen 2.5: excels at APIs, snippets, refactors, and technical explanations in the same ChatML framing as the general Qwen instruct models. Less ideal than general Qwen or Mistral for purely marketing or literary prose where a non-code prior helps tone.
models.license_note: Apache-2.0 — Qwen2.5-Coder; see Alibaba model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: Google’s tiny instruction-tuned Gemma 2—very fast on laptops and fine for light Q&A. Noticeably weaker than 7B+ models on complex reasoning, long answers, and delicate German phrasing; prefer Gemma 9B or Qwen if quality matters more than speed.
models.license_note: Gemma license — see Google Gemma terms on Hugging Face model card.

models.description: Google’s mid-size Gemma 2 instruct model: balanced safety, clarity, and general writing quality rivaling other strong 9B-class weights. Still a step behind Qwen 14B on the hardest mixed-language or long-context tasks when your machine can load the bigger file.
models.license_note: Gemma license — see Google Gemma terms on Hugging Face model card.

models.description: Moonshot’s Moonlight MoE activates a subset of experts per token—aims for large-model capability with moderate active compute. Can match or beat many 7B dense models on some prompts, but MoE memory patterns are trickier than a flat Qwen 14B and edge-case behavior varies more.
